interest: This file provides a clear illustration of how domestic American commercial and agricultural interests utilized congressional and diplomatic channels to gather foreign economic intelligence during the interwar period. It highlights Michigan Senator Arthur Vandenberg's advocacy on behalf of regional agricultural businesses—the Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association and the Larrowe Milling Company—seeking data on Japanese beet pulp production. Additionally, it reveals the interconnected nature of international trade at the time, explicitly referencing the Mitsubishi Trading Company's New York office as a primary resource for commercial information on Japanese agribusiness.
overview: This file comprises the U.S. State Department's 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.61353, indexing correspondence and reporting on the beet sugar and beet pulp industry in Japan. It documents an inquiry initiated on February 2 by U.S. Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg of Michigan on behalf of the Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association and the Larrowe Milling Company of Detroit requesting a report on Japanese beet pulp production. The Department subsequently instructed the American Consulate General in Tokyo to prepare the requested study, leading to the submission on March 29 of Special Report Despatch No. 1038 by the Tokyo Consulate (noting that further details could be obtained from the Mitsubishi Trading Company in New York), which was transmitted to Senator Vandenberg on April 30.

subfiles.summary: This List of Papers docket sheet records incoming and outgoing communications between February and April regarding the beet pulp and beet sugar industry in Japan under decimal file 894.61353. It tracks an inquiry from Senator Arthur Vandenberg forwarding a request from the Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association and Larrowe Milling Company, instructions sent by the Department to the Tokyo Consulate, and the subsequent transmission of Tokyo Despatch No. 1038 back to the Department and to Senator Vandenberg. The entries note that further commercial information could be obtained through the Mitsubishi Trading Company in New York.
